messages.subject: Monitor resources by attribute
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

At our hospital, we're simulating patient flow through several resources (clinic, IC, day treatment, OR). The patients have an attribute patient_group, which determines arrival rate, length of stay, and trajectories.

Does simmer have a way to monitor the usage of the four resources by attribute? For example, I might be interested in how many patients from group 1 are using the clinic resource.

Currently, I extract arrivals and attributes, join them together, and use the code below to calculate resource usage. This works, but it's pretty slow.

Thanks in advance!
Arnoud Plantinga

# Create one row per patient per hour
ind_usage <- arrivals_attributes %>%
mutate.(time = map2.(start_time, end_time, `:`)) %>%
unnest.(time)

# Count usage
usage_counts <- ind_usage %>%
count.(replication, time, resource, patient_group,
  name = "usage"
)

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Monitor resources by attribute
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Thu, 14 Oct 2021 at 15:58, Arnoud Plantinga <arno...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> At our hospital, we're simulating patient flow through several resources (clinic, IC, day treatment, OR). The patients have an attribute patient_group, which determines arrival rate, length of stay, and trajectories.
>
> Does simmer have a way to monitor the usage of the four resources by attribute? For example, I might be interested in how many patients from group 1 are using the clinic resource.

# Option 1: auxiliary resources. For example:

group <- function(n) trajectory() %>%
  seize(paste0("some_resource_queue_", n)) %>%
  seize("some_resource") %>%
  release(paste0("some_resource_queue_", n)) %>%
  seize(paste0("some_resource_server_", n)) %>%
  timeout(function() rexp(1, 1)) %>%
  release_all()

env <- simmer() %>%
  add_resource("some_resource", 1) %>%
  add_resource(paste0("some_resource_queue_", 1:2), Inf) %>%
  add_resource(paste0("some_resource_server_", 1:2), Inf) %>%
  add_generator("group1_", group(1), function() rexp(1, 0.2)) %>%
  add_generator("group2_", group(2), function() rexp(1, 0.3)) %>%
  run(1000)

get_mon_resources(env)

# Option 2: auxiliary globals. For example:

group <- function(n) trajectory() %>%
  set_global(paste0("some_resource_queue_", n), 1, mod="+") %>%
  seize("some_resource") %>%
  set_global(paste0("some_resource_queue_", n), -1, mod="+") %>%
  set_global(paste0("some_resource_server_", n), 1, mod="+") %>%
  timeout(function() rexp(1, 1)) %>%
  set_global(paste0("some_resource_server_", n), -1, mod="+") %>%
  release("some_resource")

env <- simmer() %>%
  add_resource("some_resource", 1) %>%
  add_generator("group1_", group(1), function() rexp(1, 0.2), mon=2) %>%
  add_generator("group2_", group(2), function() rexp(1, 0.3), mon=2) %>%
  run(1000)

get_mon_attributes(env)

---

Of course, if you are only interested in the queue or in the server, the code above can be further simplified.

Hope it helps,
Iñaki

messages.subject: Renege-Timer releasing wrong resource?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

 I'm tearing my hair out and struggling to debug this one.

 I have extended my ICU model (
https://github.com/ConnectedBradford/ICU-Model ) to have multiple ICUs
(each with their own "halfnurse" resource)

 I am getting errors like:

Error: 'Renege-Timer' at 19001.71:
 'BRI halfnurse' not previously seized

(from variable trajectories, and with variable halfnurses)
I can't tell exactly which arrival it's coming from, but I can see
that there is no arrival at that point that should have "BRI
halfnurse" seized - the most recent attempts to seize a halfnurse are
from other ICUs.

 Halfnurses are seized as either 1 or 2 halfnurses depending on the
needs of the patient.
 If I set the capacity to infinite the problem goes away

The halfnurses are seized by:
    seize_selected( function() {
      print(paste0(sources[get_attribute(env,"source")]," halfnurse"))
      if (get_attribute(env,"lvl_start")==3) 2 else 1
    })
(the print is part of debugging attempts)

Any ideas where to look? I'm trying to create a reproducible example
but it's data-driven and the data is unfortunately not publishable.

thanks!

tom

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: Renege-Timer releasing wrong resource?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom,

On Wed, 20 Oct 2021 at 22:14, Tom Lawton <t...@t-lawton.org> wrote:
>
> I'm very confused - I switched round the order of the seizing and now
> it works fine.

Great!

> For my understanding - does the fact that the error comes from
> "Renege-Timer" mean that it's produced when reneging tries to release
> all resources?

Yes, it does. The "not previously seized" messages, in general,
shouldn't happen (unless you actively call release without a previous
seize), which indicates that there may be a bug. It would be nice to
have a reproducible example.

> On Wed, Oct 20, 2021 at 5:48 PM Tom Lawton <t...@t-lawton.org> wrote:
> >
> > Hi,
> >
> >  I'm tearing my hair out and struggling to debug this one.
> >
> >  I have extended my ICU model (
> > https://github.com/ConnectedBradford/ICU-Model ) to have multiple ICUs
> > (each with their own "halfnurse" resource)

Are there clone() instructions involved in this extended model? We
have seen there are some issues with clones, especially with nested
clones (clone of a clone), but it may not be the case here.

> >  [snip]

> >
> > Any ideas where to look? I'm trying to create a reproducible example
> > but it's data-driven and the data is unfortunately not publishable.

Is the model shareable? At least the specific part involved and the
surroundings. You can set simmer(verbose=TRUE) to get a trace of the
low-level events. It would be nice if you could share the last part of
that (not the entire trace, because the data *could* be reconstructed
using that).

--
Iñaki Úcar

messages.body_plain:
Thanks - glad I'm not going insane! No clones used (though if #207 is
added then I'd like to have parallel queueing one day)

Verbose trace attached - from the initial arrival of Patient505 who
appears to be the one with the issue. I've also attached the code,
though unfortunately not the data it uses. The crash is pretty
reliable so I could probably produce some fake data that would trigger
it.
Interestingly the crash doesn't occur if I change the order of seizing
in the initial_seize trajectory
Presently - bed, L3bed, halfnurse = crash
Change to bed, halfnurse, L3bed = no crash

Halfnurse is the only resource that an arrival will ever seize two of
- then releasing them one at a time

tom
